result.description: Open-source WordPress ecommerce plugin; REST API exposes store data (orders, products, customers, coupons, etc.) per self-hosted store.
result.auth_detail: No OAuth2 on the REST API. HTTPS: HTTP Basic with Consumer Key/Secret. HTTP: OAuth 1.0a one-legged (HMAC signature scheme, not OAuth2). The MCP server uses WordPress Application Passwords, not OAuth2 or REST keys.
result.access_detail: Self-hosted plugin. Store owner generates consumer key/secret in their own store admin, with no vendor approval. Each store has its own base URL and credentials. Pricing/plan gating was not checked, so the free-access claim is inferred from the self-hosted model.
result.api_notes: REST v3 at /wp-json/wc/v3/. Covers coupons, customers, orders, order notes, refunds, products, variations, categories, tags, reviews, reports, tax, webhooks, settings, payment gateways, shipping zones, system status, data.
result.blocker: No OAuth2. Users must supply store URL plus consumer key/secret. Store must serve HTTPS for Basic auth. The official MCP is in developer preview, needs the MCP Adapter plugin, and authenticates with Application Passwords.

evidence.quote: WooCommerce (WC) 2.6+ is fully integrated with the WordPress REST API.
You may use HTTP Basic Auth by providing the REST API Consumer Key as the username and the REST API Consumer Secret as the password.
You must use OAuth 1.0a "one-legged" authentication to ensure REST API credentials cannot be intercepted by an attacker.
WooCommerce includes two ways to authenticate with the WP REST API.
The current WP REST API integration version is `v3` which takes a first-order position in endpoints.
The MCP implementation in WooCommerce is currently in developer preview.
Remote HTTP connections authenticate using a WordPress username and an Application Password.
